title: Hidden architecture and the thermodynamic cost of an exact stochastic signal
shortTitle: Same signal, less dissipation: hidden architecture matters
oneLine: The smallest hidden Markov model that reproduces an exactly known two-level signal can overstate its least possible dissipation: a four-state mechanism produces exactly the same signal as every three-state one yet dissipates strictly less, and a sharp floor holds for any hidden size.
abstract: Experiments often see only a coarse two-level signal produced by a hidden Markov network of unknown size, and one model-based way to bound its dissipation is to fit the smallest hidden model that reproduces the signal and minimise entropy production over it. This candidate shows by an exact example that the procedure can overstate the least possible dissipation even when the signal is known perfectly. For a binary alternating-renewal family P_q (0 < q < 1), three hidden states are the fewest that realise the signal and the exact three-state entropy minimum is (1−q)log(1/q), attained uniquely by the homogeneous driven ring; for every q an explicit finite four-state model reproduces the same complete stationary observed law with strictly less entropy production. At q = 1/20 exact rational models have certified costs 2.7730766578…, 2.7659977105… (four states) and 2.7469854029… (five states), all below the three-state minimum 2.8459456598…. Over all finite architectures matching only the entrance intensity r, mean complete dwell m and initial dwell density f₀, the exact entropy infimum is 4r√(1−mf₀) artanh√(1−mf₀) when 0 < mf₀ < 1, approached by three-state models and attained by none; for mf₀ ≥ 1 a reversible model attains zero. For the benchmark this floor is about 108 times the one certified in an earlier Evidence Press candidate. The exact four-state and unrestricted minima remain open. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

keyResults: Three hidden states are the fewest that produce the signal P_q, and the exact three-state minimum entropy production is (1−q)log(1/q), attained uniquely by the homogeneous driven ring (Theorem 1, proof).
For every 0 < q < 1 an explicit four-state model reproduces exactly the same complete observed law and dissipates strictly less: V₄(P_q) < V₃(P_q) (Theorem 1, proof).

At q = 1/20, exact rational models cost 2.7730766578… and 2.7659977105… with four states and 2.7469854029… with five, against 2.8459456598… for any three-state model (Theorem 1, Proposition 6, exact certificates).

For any hidden size, entropy production exceeds 4r√(1−mf₀) artanh√(1−mf₀) when 0 < mf₀ < 1, with no renewal assumption; this is the exact infimum given (r, m, f₀) and is attained by no finite model (Theorems 2 and 5, proof).
Hence (2/3)(1−q)log(1/q) ≤ V∞(P_q) ≤ V₄(P_q) < V₃(P_q); at q = 1/20 the floor 1.8973 is about 108 times the earlier certified floor (Corollary 4).
Numerically the four-state optimum at q = 1/20 is about 2.765996 and a fifth state lowers the cost further (Section 6, numerical only); the exact V₄ and V∞ remain open.

narration: Does the simplest model of a hidden process tell you its least possible energy cost? An Evidence Press briefing. First, the background. Many experiments on single molecules see only a coarse signal: an ion channel is open or shut, a motor is bound or unbound. Behind that signal is a hidden network of molecular states, and keeping it running dissipates energy. A common way to put a lower bound on that cost is to fit the smallest hidden model that reproduces the signal, and ask how little that model could dissipate. Now, the main finding. That shortcut is not safe, even when the signal is known perfectly. For a family of exactly specified two-level signals, the paper proves that three hidden states are the fewest that can produce the signal, and finds the cheapest three-state mechanism: a simple driven ring. It then builds a four-state mechanism that produces exactly the same signal and dissipates strictly less. At one benchmark, exact models with four and five states lower the cost from about 2.85 to 2.77, and then to 2.75, in natural units. The paper also proves a floor that holds however many hidden states there are, using just three features of the observed signal. For the benchmark, that floor is about 108 times the one certified in an earlier Evidence Press release. Why might this matter? Reported dissipation bounds can depend on an arbitrary choice of model size, so they may be too high. Readers can rerun the exact certificates, which need only standard Python. The main limitation: the true minimum with four states, or with any number, is still unknown. Finally, the status. This is an anonymous, unrefereed candidate, checked by AI-assisted review only, not peer review. It was published on 28 October 2026; its paper and evidence are linked from the Evidence Press release page. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.

decisionObject.description: An exact four-state realisation of the complete observed law P_q with strictly less entropy production than every three-state realisation, for every 0 < q < 1, showing that the minimal hidden model does not certify the thermodynamic minimum; plus a sharp architecture-independent floor.
